paper_metadata.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper surveys more than 300 methods for automatic knowledge graph construction, organizing the field into knowledge acquisition, knowledge refinement, and knowledge evolution. It reviews entity discovery and linking, coreference resolution, relation extraction, graph completion, knowledge fusion, conditional knowledge acquisition and completion, and knowledge dynamics, and discusses resources, challenges, and future directions.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses the need for a systematic organization of automatic knowledge graph construction methods that can transform heterogeneous, semi-structured, and unstructured data into conceptualized structured knowledge, while also refining and evolving existing graphs in complex big-data environments.

methodology.description: This is a broad narrative survey rather than a single Text-to-KG system. It defines knowledge graph construction as mapping data sources plus background knowledge into graphs, then organizes reviewed methods in execution and lifecycle order: semi-structured preprocessing; knowledge acquisition through entity discovery, typing, linking, coreference resolution, and relation extraction; knowledge refinement through completion and fusion; knowledge evolution through conditional and temporal knowledge methods; storage; and open research directions. The survey compares methods by data environment, motivation, and architecture.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The survey treats background knowledge as essential to knowledge graph construction. It may be supplied as pre-designed rules, an ontology, a schema, or implicit mathematical principles. The formal KG definition includes concepts, relations, factual triples, and background constraints; YAGO is cited as integrating Wikipedia with a WordNet ontology.

input_output.input_type: Heterogeneous data sources, including unstructured text, semi-structured web pages and tables, images, temporal data, and existing knowledge graphs.
input_output.input_granularity: The reviewed methods operate over web pages, table forms, sentences, textual documents, long cross-sentence or cross-paragraph contexts, and existing graph structures.
input_output.output_representation: Intermediate outputs include cleaned documents, entity mentions and types, linked entities, coreference pairs or clusters, relations, and factual triples. Final outputs include raw, refined, fused, complete, conditional, temporal, dynamic, and stored knowledge graphs.

Pretrained and graph-based approaches: BERT and graph convolutional networks
Knowledge refinement tools: OpenKE, OpenEA, OpenNE, and Falcon-AO

Reviewed model families for NER, entity typing, entity linking, coreference resolution, open and domain-specific relation extraction, distant supervision, few-shot extraction, joint extraction, document-level extraction, completion, fusion, and temporal/dynamic KGs

value: The survey covers more than 300 knowledge graph construction methods.

It organizes KG construction into knowledge acquisition, knowledge refinement, and knowledge evolution, with detailed coverage of entity discovery, coreference resolution, relation extraction, completion, fusion, condition knowledge, and knowledge dynamics.

It identifies a progression from rule- and pattern-based information extraction toward statistical, neural, pretrained, graph-based, joint, few-shot, document-level, interpretable, multimodal, federated, and end-to-end approaches.
The survey provides practical KG projects, datasets, tools, architecture summaries, and a discussion of challenges in heterogeneous, autonomous, complex, and evolving data environments.

code_and_data_availability: The paper does not report survey-specific code or a dedicated released dataset. It provides access links for numerous existing KG projects and off-the-shelf tools, including datasets such as YAGO, Freebase, DBpedia, Wikidata, ASER, TransOMCS, and OpenKG.cn, and tools such as TextRunner, spaCy, OpenNRE, gBuilder, OpenKE, and OpenEA.
